newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ at a cyclical low for contrarians -Cavill White.
newsitem.headline: NZ at a cyclical low for contrarians -Cavill White.

text.p: New Zealand's sluggish economy is good for bonds but tough for equities, Cavill White principal Don Turkington said in the brokers' latest economic report.
He said export stocks may see some recovery as the New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index eased on the back of lower rates in coming months.
The government's fiscal stance would be important in ensuring monetary conditions were not tightened before growth picked up, Turkington added.
"For the contrarian investor, New Zealand offers what appears to be a cyclical low," he said in Wednesday's report.
"While interest rates will help, it is not yet clear, however, what will trigger a cyclical recovery," he said.
The decline in domestic demand had been deeper and more prolonged than most had projected.
Recovery in economic activity and corporate profitability, tipped to be under way by now, had been pushed out into the future.
"Government economic policy remains something of a mystery, with all eyes being focussed on the coalition's first budget on June 26.
"That budget may help establish the government's economic style but it should not be relied upon to kick start the economy," he said.
The Reserve Bank's monetary policy statement on June 27 is expected to signal an easing in policy, he said.
Confirmiaton of declining interest rates would be positive for the economy and was a necessary condition for equities to perform.
Cyclical commodity-oriented stocks would continue to receive support and the attractiveness of bonds should heighten as inflationary pressured eased, he said.
"The brave may consider selective buying of domestic stocks, with the proviso that the timing of any upturn remains anyone's guess," Turkington concluded.
